adequacy_test.fitted_scale: ln(spread), so the rate that _payback compounds is the rate that was estimated
adequacy_test.inference_unit: distinct rate CHANGES, not statement prints: a tariff reprinted unchanged is not a second observation of the price
adequacy_test.spread_rule: both cells adequate AND the full-window 95% CI excludes zero AND the post-break refit agrees in sign and is itself adequate AND the post-break CI still excludes zero after being widened for having chosen the breakpoint from the data

because: the full-window slope does not survive the structural-break check: it is carried by a single step of $0.04844/kWh on 2025-06-11 (21.4% of the prior level), not by an ongoing trend

the post-break slope is significant on its own interval ([1.89, 20.81]%/yr) but not once that interval is widened for having CHOSEN the breakpoint from the data ([-6.9, 32.22]%/yr over 4 candidate steps). 4 independent rate changes cannot support a trend claim once breakpoint selection is paid for

summer.ci_basis: escalation_pct_yr, escalation_ci95_pct_yr and excludes_zero come from the ln(spread) fit, which is what gates the verdict and what _payback compounds. slope_usd_kwh_per_yr and slope_ci95 are the descriptive linear fit; on a non-monotonic history the two scales can disagree, so do not read excludes_zero against slope_ci95.
not_determined_because: the full-window slope does not survive the structural-break check: it is carried by a single step of $0.04844/kWh on 2025-06-11 (21.4% of the prior level), not by an ongoing trend

post_break.ci_basis: escalation_pct_yr, escalation_ci95_pct_yr and excludes_zero come from the ln(spread) fit, which is what gates the verdict and what _payback compounds. slope_usd_kwh_per_yr and slope_ci95 are the descriptive linear fit; on a non-monotonic history the two scales can disagree, so do not read excludes_zero against slope_ci95.

would_settle_it: More rate CHANGES, not more statements: the interval is set by the 3 distinct spreads in the window, and reprinting the same tariff adds none. At roughly two delivery redesigns a year, a corpus reaching into 2028 would roughly double the independent units.

A breakpoint fixed in advance from published tariff effective dates rather than chosen as the largest observed step. That removes the selection penalty entirely and the unadjusted interval becomes legitimate.
Statements from before 2024-05-25, which would extend the pre-break window and let the two segments be compared as a formal change-point model rather than a refit.

inputs.exclusion_rule: rate_per_kwh == 0 with kwh <= 0 is a NEM export settlement deferral, not a price. Asserted, not assumed: a zero on positive kwh aborts the run.

all_in_spread.reason: The all-in on-peak price is delivery plus generation. With generation undetermined past the provider break, an all-in spread trend would splice a charged tariff to a comparison figure across 72% of the corpus.

generation_escalation.reason: On a CCA date this corpus carries no charged generation tariff. The printed generation table is SDG&E's bundled comparison, off the actual CEA charge by -6.8% to +104.3% (issue #3). The provider broke on 2024-12-27, leaving 547 of 763 corpus days (2024-05-25..2026-06-26) with no charged generation price.
would_settle_it: The CCA's own per-TOU rates, which appear only on the CCA pages of the statements; parse_bills.py does not extract those pages.
A second bundled-era stretch long enough to fit generation separately -- the corpus has only 216 bundled days.
